topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate
sections.content: Briefly recall that a derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change (the slope of a tangent line). Visualize a drone flying: the derivative of its position over time is its velocity.
sections.example: A drone moving along a 1D track. At any moment, the speedometer reading is the derivative of its position function.

sections.title: The Inverse Operation: Accumulation
sections.content: Introduce the integral as the 'accumulation' of changes. If the derivative tells us how fast we are changing, the integral adds up all those tiny changes to find the total displacement.
sections.example: If you know the drone's velocity at every moment, integrating that velocity function 'sums up' the tiny distances to show the drone's total change in position.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Visualized)
sections.content: Explain the core relationship: differentiation and integration are inverse processes (like multiplication and division). Show an animation where a function is sliced into thin rectangles (integral) and then compressed back into the slope of a curve (derivative).
sections.example: Think of a 'magic fountain': The rate at which water pours out (derivative) determines the height of the water level in the tank (integral). If you change the pour rate, the water level changes accordingly.

sections.title: Synthesis and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize that F'(x) = f(x) and the integral of f(x) is F(x) + C. Emphasize that the integral 'reconstructs' the function from its rate of change.
sections.example: A smart thermostat: The 'derivative' is the change in room temperature per minute; the 'integral' of that change tells the system the total temperature shift since it was turned on.
